q: 1. A scale which has a common representative fraction, but read in different measures, is called a
explain: A comparative scale shares the same representative fraction as another scale but is graduated in a different unit of measurement (e.g., miles and kilometres), enabling direct comparison.

q: 2. An average length of a pace is
explain: An average human pace (step length) while walking normally is taken as approximately 0.8 m (80 cm) for rough distance estimation in surveying.

q: 3. The least count of a vernier scale is
options: sum of the smallest division of main and vernier scales
value of one division of the primary scale divided by total number of division of vernier scale
value of one division of vernire scale divided by total number of division of primary scale
explain: Least count of a vernier = (value of one main scale division) / (total number of divisions on the vernier scale); this is the smallest reading directly obtainable with the vernier.

q: 4. On a diagonal scale, it is possible to read up to
explain: A diagonal scale uses primary divisions, sub-divisions, and diagonal lines to allow three successive dimensions to be read directly, e.g. units, tenths and hundredths.

q: 5. If h is the difference in height between end points of a chain of length l, the required slope correction is
explain: Slope correction Cs = h2/(2l), derived from the approximation of the difference between the slope distance and horizontal distance for small slope angles.

q: 6. Accidental or compensating errors of length L are proportional to
explain: Accidental errors tend to partly cancel each other, so their cumulative effect over a distance L grows in proportion to the square root of L, not L itself.

q: 7. While measuring a chain line between two stations intervened by a raised ground
options: both vision and chaining get obstructed
explain: A raised ground (hillock) between two intervisible-but-blocked stations obstructs the line of sight between them, while the chain can still be laid along the ground; hence only vision is obstructed.

q: 8. In chain surveying tie lines are primarily provided
options: to check the accuracy of the survey
to take offsets for detail survey
to avoid long offsets from chain lines
to increase the number of chain lines
explain: Tie lines join subsidiary points on the main survey lines so that offsets to detail near them remain short and manageable, avoiding the errors of very long offsets.

q: 9. An instrument used for ranging is
explain: A line ranger is an instrument specifically designed to establish intermediate points in line between two stations that may not be intervisible, i.e., for ranging.

q: 10. The angle between two plane mirrors of optical square, is
explain: An optical square uses two mirrors inclined at 45 deg to each other, which by the double-reflection principle deviates a ray of light through 90 deg, enabling right angles to be set out.

q: 11. Number of links per metre length of a chain are
explain: In a standard metric chain, there are 5 links per metre length, so a 20 m chain has 100 links and a 30 m chain has 150 links.

q: 12. Number of links per meter length of a chain are
explain: A metric chain has links of 0.2 m each, so there are 5 links per metre length of the chain.

q: 13. If L is the specified length of a tape, L1 its actual length and S the measured distance, then true distance is given by the formula
explain: As per the book's answer key, the true distance correction formula given is ((L-L1)/L) x S, representing the proportional correction applied for the discrepancy between nominal and actual tape length.

q: 14. Ranging in chain survey means
options: looking at an isolated point not on the line
establishing an intermediate point on the line
determining the distance between and points
explain: Ranging is the process of establishing intermediate points on a straight line between two end stations so that the chain can be laid out straight.

q: 15. A check line in a chain surveying
options: checks the accuracy of the framework
enables the surveyor to locate the interior details which are far away from the main chain lines
fixed up the directions of all other lines
explain: A check line, by connecting two known points on the main framework and being independently measured, checks accuracy, helps in locating interior details, and helps verify directions - so all of the above apply.

q: 16. The instrument used for setting out an offset at a right angle, is called
explain: An open cross-staff is the simplest instrument with two pairs of slits at right angles, used specifically for setting out offsets at 90 degrees to the chain line.

q: 17. The adjustable cross-staff is used for setting out an offset
explain: Unlike the fixed open or french cross-staff, the adjustable cross-staff has a rotatable upper part, allowing offsets to be set out at any desired angle.

q: 18. For setting out an offset at an angle 45, ... cross-staff is used
explain: A french cross-staff has slits set at both 90 degrees and 45 degrees, making it specifically suited for setting out offsets at 45 degrees to the chain line.

q: 19. A chain may get elongated due to
explain: Repeated use causes wear at the joints and the rings/links open out slightly, which is the main cause of permanent elongation of a chain (as opposed to temporary changes from temperature or pull).

q: 20. Handles of chains are made up of
explain: The handles of a surveying chain are usually made of brass (a non-magnetic, corrosion resistant material), while the links themselves are of steel or galvanized iron.

q: 21. The length of an Engineer's chain is
explain: An Engineer's chain is 100 feet long, divided into 100 links of 1 foot each, distinguishing it from Gunter's chain (66 feet).

q: 22. Ceylon Ghat tracer can read slopes up to
explain: The Ceylon ghat tracer, designed for locating contour gradients on steep hill roads, can read slope ratios ranging from about 1 in 120 to 1 in 6.

q: 23. The index glass in an optical square is
options: one-fourth silvered and half un silvered
half silvered and half un silvered
explain: The index glass in an optical square is wholly silvered, so it fully reflects the image of the object sighted through it towards the horizon glass.

q: 24. The instrument, belonging to a class of reflecting instrument is
explain: The box sextant works on the principle of double reflection from two mirrors, making it a reflecting instrument, unlike the line ranger or prismatic compass.

q: 25. In an optical square, the angle between the first incident ray and the last reflected ray is
explain: Due to the 45-degree angle between the two mirrors and the principle of double reflection, the optical square deflects the incident ray through exactly 90 degrees.

q: 26. Check lines (or proof lines) in Chain Surveying are essentially required
options: to indicate the accuracy of the survey work
explain: Check lines are measured independently in the field specifically to verify (indicate) the accuracy of the main chain survey framework after plotting.

q: 27. The limiting length of an offset does not depend upon
explain: As per the book's answer key, the limiting length of an offset depends on the accuracy required, the method of setting out perpendiculars, and the nature of features surveyed - but not on the scale of plotting.

q: 28. The angle between two plane mirrors of optical square is
explain: The two plane mirrors in an optical square are fixed at exactly 45 degrees to each other to achieve a 90-degree deflection of the line of sight.

q: 29. For taking offsets with an optical square on the right hand side of the chain line, it is held
explain: For an object on the right side of the chain line, the optical square is conventionally held in the right hand, upright, for correct sighting.

q: 30. The maximum allowable limit up to that a measurement may vary from the true value is known as
explain: The permissible error is defined as the maximum allowable deviation of a measured value from its true value, within the specified precision of the survey.

q: 31. An obstacle which obstructs both chaining and ranging may be
explain: A building lying directly in the path of a survey line obstructs both the direct line of sight (ranging) and the physical laying of the chain (chaining) across it.

q: 32. In order to locate a point by oblique offsets we must measure and note at least
explain: Locating a point by the method of oblique offsets requires measuring two distances (offsets) from two different points on the chain line to the detail point.

q: 33. The most accurate measurement of the length of a long survey lines is made by using?
explain: Electronic Distance Measuring (EDM) equipment provides the highest accuracy for measuring the length of long survey lines, superior to steel bands, invar tapes, or tacheometry.

q: 34. Ranging is the process of
options: fixing ranging rods on the extremities of area
aligning the chain in a straight line between two extremities
taking offsets from a chain line
chaining over a range of mountains
explain: Ranging is the process of establishing and aligning intermediate points in a straight line between two extremities (end stations) of a chain line, so measurements can proceed along a true line.

q: 35. The obstacle, which obstructs chaining but not vision is a
explain: A river obstructs physical chaining across it (since the chain cannot be laid through water) but does not block the line of sight between the two banks, allowing indirect measurement methods.

q: 36. Hypotenusal allowance is
explain: The hypotenusal allowance, used to account for the extra length measured along a slope compared to the horizontal, is given by (sec theta - 1) multiplied by the measured (sloped) distance.

q: 37. Measuring with a 30 m chain, 0.01 m too short, introduces
explain: A chain that is shorter than its nominal length causes each measured chain length to record slightly more than the true distance, leading to a positive cumulative error that grows with the number of chain lengths measured.

q: 38. The maximum tolerance in 20 m chain is
explain: The permissible tolerance limit for a 20 m surveying chain in overall length is ±5 mm, as per standard specifications.

q: 39. The length of chain is measured from
options: center of one handle to center of other handle
outside of one handle to outside of other handle
outside of one handle to inside of other handle
inside of one handle to inside of other handle
explain: The nominal length of a surveying chain is measured from the centre of one handle to the centre of the other handle at the opposite end.

q: 40. The principle of chain surveying is to divided the area into a number of
explain: The fundamental principle of chain surveying is to divide the area into a series of well-conditioned triangles, since a triangle is the only simple plane figure that can be plotted uniquely from its three side lengths alone.

q: 41. If the chain line which runs along N-S direction is horizontal and the ground in E-W direction is sloping
options: it is possible to set offsets correctly on east side
it is possible to set offsets correctly on east side
it is not possible to set offsets correctly on west side
it is possible to set offsets correctly on both sides
explain: As per the book's answer key, when the ground slopes in the E-W direction while the chain line is horizontal (N-S), it is not possible to correctly set offsets on the west side using simple methods, due to the sloping perpendicular direction.

q: 42. If a chain is used at a temperature ... the temperature at which it was calibrated, the error in measured length is negative
explain: If the chain is used at a temperature lower than its calibration temperature, the chain contracts slightly (becomes shorter than nominal), causing the measured length to be recorded as greater than the true length - a negative error in the corrected sense.

q: 43. The error in measured length due to sag of chain or tape is known as
explain: Sag causes the measured tape/chain length to record a distance longer than the true straight-line distance, resulting in a negative error requiring subtraction.

q: 44. If L is the distance between two supports from which a tape is suspended under a pull P and W is the total weight of the tape the sag correction is
explain: The standard sag correction formula for a tape freely suspended between two supports under pull P with total weight W is (L/24)(W/P)^2.

q: 45. If the length of a chain line along a slope of theta is l, the required slope correction is
explain: The slope correction to be subtracted from a chain line of length l measured along a slope of angle theta is given by the formula 2l sin^2(theta/2).

q: 46. Prolongation of chain line across an obstruction in chain surveying, is done by
explain: Prolonging a chain line across an obstruction can be achieved using any of several field methods together - angular measurements, constructing perpendiculars, or solving triangles - so all of the above are valid techniques.

q: 47. A clinometer is used for
explain: A clinometer's specific and sole function is to measure the angle of slope (inclination) of the ground or a line of sight.
